purpose: Visual criticism of classic-series place identity, not a game asset pack. References retain their original rights.
capture: References are browser screenshots of observed photographs/frames, not AI illustrations. Native game PNGs are separate, unmodified 256x192 captures.

sources.version: Original production designer Richard Hoover: S1/S2 Double R set photograph; not the Pilot exterior and not a modern cafe tour.
Hoover sheriff reception set photograph. Partial room evidence: does not establish Truman's office layout.
Hoover Great Northern check-in set photograph. Authored motifs are evidence of visual identity, not permission to invent a new floorplan.
Hoover Great Northern fireplace set photograph.
Hoover Roadhouse set photograph. The upper gallery is visible; camera projection differs from the game.
Pilot broadcast living-room frame. The article's 2019 location photographs are not used as the bar.
Pilot broadcast reverse view: upholstered sitting group and paired oval mirrors.
Pilot portrait detail, supporting reference; not a replacement for the whole-room view.
S2E1 opening broadcast frame, low camera and partial geometry. Supports timber material comparison, not a complete room plan or an inferred fireplace.
Published broadcast furnishing frame. Exact episode not independently established: score applies to visible curtain/floor/furniture grammar, not continuity of a particular episode.
Pilot broadcast exterior, not the rebuilt modern Twede's facade.
Pilot broadcast establishing frame: lodge above the waterfall. Replaces the temporarily disputed closer facade view.
S2E22 broadcast morning frame. Caption 2022 is an episode identifier, not the photograph's year. No direct day/night color penalty.
